prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1010; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports a concussion and headaches. Claimant is represented by counsel; all contact to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Confirmed representation letter received. Attorney requests that no direct contact be made with the claimant. Asked for medical authorization forms and a copy of the emergency room record. Attorney states treatment is ongoing with a neurologist.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of both vehicles. Rear bumper and tailgate damage on the claimant's vehicle, consistent with a moderate-speed impact. Third-party driver's statement acknowledges failing to stop in time. Liability appears clear. Repair estimate requested from the preferred shop.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the emergency department. Diagnosis listed as concussion with post-impact headaches and dizziness. Follow-up imaging was ordered. Attorney's office sent a demand package outlining lost wages and ongoing symptoms. Reserve reviewed and adjusted for bodily injury exposure. Referred file to the injury unit for evaluation.

Entry 5: Injury unit reviewed records and requested an independent neurological review. Attorney notified of the request and agreed to schedule. Property damage payment issued to the repair shop once the estimate was approved. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days pending the independent review results.
